### Trusting Your Own Instincts
Author: Stuart Briscoe (One Year Devotions for Men)
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/trusting-your-own-instincts-one-year-devotions-for-men-september-9.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 8:7
Points:
- Human beings often trust their own instincts rather than adhering to God's revealed instructions.
- Israel envied the visible military power and less demanding religions of their pagan neighbors.
- Demanding an earthly king signaled that Israel was abandoning faith in God for human self-reliance.
- God warned Israel about the cost of a human monarch, yet allowed them to face the consequences of their decision.
- Believers must submit personal desires to God's sovereignty instead of placing confidence in earthly substitutes.

### Be Careful What You Ask For
Author: Alistair Begg (Truth For Life)
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-may-29-2025.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 8:7-9
Points:
- Israel wanted to assimilate into the surrounding pagan cultures instead of remaining set apart under God's rule.
- Insisting on an earthly judge and ruler was an outright rejection of God's kingship.
- God's willingness to grant Israel a king served as judgment, allowing them to experience the painful burden of their choice.
- Sin often acts as its own punishment when God lets people have what they wrongly demand.
- True divine mercy is displayed when God withholds harmful desires and provides the King we truly need in Jesus Christ.
